description: The first of the marfūʿ (nominative) noun categories: the fāʿil, the doer of the verb's action.

lessons.titleEnglish: The Definition of al-Fāʿil and Its Two Kinds
lessons.matnArabic: الْفَاعِلُ: هُوَ الِاسْمُ الْمَرْفُوعُ الْمَذْكُورُ قَبْلَهُ فِعْلُهُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: ظَاهِرٌ وَمُضْمَرٌ.
lessons.translation: The fāʿil is the noun in the nominative case that is mentioned [in a sentence] after its verb [comes before it]. It is of two kinds: apparent (ẓāhir) and hidden/pronominal (muḍmar).
lessons.explanation: This opens the long section of al-Ājurrūmiyyah dealing one by one with every category of marfūʿ noun (مرفوعات الأسماء) - the fāʿil is the first and most fundamental. Three things are packed into the definition: it must be an ism (never a verb or particle), it must be marfūʿ, and the normal Arabic sentence order places the verb first and the fāʿil after it (unlike English, where the subject usually comes first). A فاعل ظاهر is an explicit noun like زيد in قامَ زيدٌ; a فاعل مضمر is a hidden pronoun folded into the verb itself, as in قُمْتُ ('I stood'), where the doer 'I' is not a separate word but the تُ attached to the verb.

keyTerms.definition: The marfūʿ noun that performs the action of the verb preceding it.
An explicit, separately-written noun functioning as the fāʿil.
A pronoun attached to or embedded within the verb itself, functioning as the fāʿil.

examples.irabAnswer: زَيْدٌ: فاعلٌ مرفوعٌ وعلامة رفعه الضمةُ الظاهرة على آخره.

examples.translation: I stood (the fāʿil here is the hidden pronoun تُ, 'I', fused into the verb).
examples.irabAnswer: التاء: ضمير متصل مبني في محل رفع فاعل.
هِنْدٌ: فاعلٌ مرفوعٌ وعلامة رفعه الضمةُ الظاهرة، والتاءُ في «قامتْ» علامة تأنيثٍ ساكنة لا محل لها من الإعراب.

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: What is the definition of الفاعل?
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: الاسم المرفوع المذكور قبله فعله (the noun in the nominative case, mentioned with its verb coming before it).

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: What are the two kinds of fāʿil, and how do they differ?
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: ظاهر (apparent) - an explicit separate noun; ومضمر (hidden) - a pronoun embedded in or attached to the verb itself.

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: In the sentence «قامَ زيدٌ», what is the grammatical role of زيدٌ?
In Arabic word order, does the fāʿil normally come before or after its verb?
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: After - the verb is normally mentioned first, then the fāʿil.

memorisationSections.translation: The fāʿil is the noun in the nominative that is mentioned after its verb. It is of two kinds: apparent and hidden.
